name: Pagaya Technologies Ltd.

profile.description: Pagaya Technologies, co-founded in 2016 by CEO Gal Krubiner, runs an AI-driven credit decisioning network that helps U.S. banks, fintechs and auto lenders approve borrowers they would otherwise decline, funding the resulting loans through asset-backed securitizations. FY2025 revenue was $1.26B (+26%) with GAAP net income of $81M, its first profitable year. Q2 2026 revenue rose 19% to $387M on $3.5B of network volume (+33%), GAAP net income nearly tripled to $45M, and full-year 2026 guidance was raised to revenue of $1.425-1.525B and GAAP net income of $155-180M.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Pagaya scaled revenue from $92M in 2020 to $1.26B in 2025 [1] and opened auto lending as a major second engine — auto volumes surged ~140% in Q2 2026 across nearly 30,000 dealerships and drove over 75% of network-volume growth [2]. AI Deployment (2/2): The entire $387M Q2 2026 revenue base flows through its proprietary AI underwriting models [2][4]. Market Share (1/2): A meaningful network across personal loans, auto and POS lending, but it competes with Upstart and bank in-house models, with no share-leadership data found. Pipeline (1/2): Raised 2026 guidance for $12.5-13.25B network volume gives visibility [2], but no named next-generation products with launch dates. R&D Intensity (0/1): FY2025 R&D of $75.2M was only ~6.0% of revenue [1], below AI-lending peers.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Pagaya's purpose — working with U.S. banks to extend loans to people who otherwise would not have access to credit, using AI to qualify them [4] — is clear and socially relevant, but not yet validated across a credit cycle. Community Impact (0/2): Financial inclusion is the business model itself; no foundation or community program with cited dollar amounts was found. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found. Insider Buying (0/2): No verified net insider buying was found in this screen's research; the Iceberg Research report alleged prior irregularities involving senior executives [5], which weighs against leadership-conviction credit.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored (Growth sleeve). Forward P/E 5.07 (1.0) [6]; forward PEG 0.15 per FMP (1.0, 2x) [1]; D/E 133.7% (0.72) [6]; ROE 19.5% (1.0, 2x) [6]; revenue growth YoY 18.6% (1.0) [6]; 5-yr revenue CAGR 68.9% derived from FMP FY2020 $91.7M to FY2025 $1.26B (1.0, 2x) [1]; profit margin 9.1% (0.46) [6]. Weighted sum 9.18/10 → 9. Liquidity cleared: 2.51M shares x $20.81 = ~$52.3M/day.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Pagaya is itself an AI company, and its moat is a lending network embedded with banks and ~30,000 auto dealerships plus years of proprietary underwriting data and securitization access [2] — AI cannot easily displace those relationships. Yet because its product is a model, it is exposed to commoditization as banks build in-house AI underwriting and rivals like Upstart compete on the same approach; FRLPC at 4.2% of network volume shows the fee take is a pressure point [2]. AI Opportunity (1/1): All revenue — $387M in Q2 2026 — is generated by AI-driven credit decisioning [2].

infinite_game.summary: Pagaya has a real cause — opening credit to people legacy scoring locks out — and a founder-led team that has stayed together since 2016 and steered the company from heavy losses to raised profit guidance. But it has never been tested by a full consumer credit downturn, and a 2025 short-seller report alleging risk-shifting onto investors and executive irregularities raises questions Sinek would want answered before calling it an infinite player.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Using AI to help banks lend to people who otherwise would not have access to credit [4] describes a future state worth working toward and is visibly lived in its partner network and auto expansion [2]. At ten years old and untested through a credit cycle, it is not yet a proven competitive advantage.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Krubiner has served as CEO and director since co-founding Pagaya in 2016 [4], giving the company leadership continuity, and he publicly framed the company's response to the October 2023 Israel war around unity and support for staff [4]. No retention or Glassdoor data was found, and Iceberg's allegations about senior executives [5] temper the score.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found acknowledging competitors such as Upstart as sources of learning; messaging centers on records, raised guidance and volume growth [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Pagaya shifted its growth engine toward auto lending, where volumes rose ~140% in Q2 2026 [2], and moved from growth-at-all-costs losses ($401M net loss in 2024) to GAAP profitability in 2025 [1] — meaningful adaptation within the same AI-underwriting model rather than a reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management cut operating expenses from $549M in 2022 to $288M in 2025 while still growing revenue [1], reaching profitability rather than chasing volume. However, Iceberg Research alleged in February 2025 that Pagaya used investor funds to absorb high-risk tranches contrary to its public risk-distribution claims [5], a question of transparency that Sinek would weigh.

investment_thesis: Pagaya has turned the corner to consistent GAAP profits: Q2 2026 revenue rose 19% to $387M, network volume grew 33% to $3.5B, GAAP net income nearly tripled to $45M, and 2026 guidance was raised to $155-180M GAAP net income and $460-490M adjusted EBITDA [2]. Revenue compounded at ~69% annually from 2020 to 2025 [1], auto lending is a powerful new engine (+~140% in Q2) [2], and the stock trades at ~5x forward earnings with a forward PEG of 0.15 [6][1].
thesis_continued: The bear case is credit-cycle and trust risk. Pagaya's network is built on borrowers that traditional models decline, so a rise in consumer delinquencies would hit both its securitization funding and its retained risk. Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $370-390M sits below the ~$398M consensus [2], FRLPC take rate of 4.2% of volume signals fee pressure [2], and D/E is ~134% [6]. Iceberg Research's 2025 allegations about risk retention and executive conduct triggered law-firm investigations [5], and the company carries a 2024 net loss of $401M as a reminder of how quickly results can swing [1].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results (expected November 2026) against guidance of $42-52M GAAP net income and $3.425-3.625B network volume [2]
Continued auto-lending expansion across ~30,000 dealerships driving network-volume growth above 30% [2]
Delivering the raised FY2026 targets ($1.425-1.525B revenue, $155-180M GAAP net income) to support re-rating from ~5x forward earnings [2][6]
key_risks: Consumer credit deterioration among near-prime borrowers impairing securitization demand and retained risk positions [2]
Governance overhang from Iceberg Research's 2025 allegations of risk-shifting to investors and executive irregularities [5]
Take-rate compression (FRLPC 4.2% of network volume) and AI-underwriting commoditization by banks and rivals like Upstart [2]
